metric.community_public_knowledge_availa.limitations: Follower/subscriber counts and Stack Overflow tag counts sourced from third-party aggregator sites (e.g. feedspot, saashub) were cross-checked but not used as a standalone score input; several general web-search results for 'r/rust subscribers' returned unrelated subreddits (the Steam game 'Rust', r/bald, r/wallstreetbets, etc.) due to name collision with the Steam survival game, and those irrelevant results were excluded from evidence rather than used to inflate or deflate the score. Numeric star/subscriber/download counts were not obtained cleanly within the 5-search budget for this shard and are therefore not asserted as point figures; the qualitative, multi-channel evidence above (official book, official multi-venue community page, weekly human-edited newsletter running continuously since 2014, official forums, Stack Overflow 'Most Loved' recognition, 90+ meetups across 35+ countries) is used instead, consistent with the rule that raw popularity counts must not be the sole proxy.
metric.community_public_knowledge_availa.selection_rule: Inspect the same knowledge channels for every language and use current, publicly accessible evidence rather than raw search-result counts alone.
